c1-12-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Not Giving Way
c1-12-01.scenario: A friend asks whether you would stop your peaceful protest if the authorities threatened you.
c1-12-01.prompt: Say that the protest goes on whatever happens, whatever the authorities threaten.
c1-12-01.target: Történjék bármi, a békés tiltakozás nem áll le. Bármilyen büntetéssel fenyegessen is a hatalom, nem hátrálunk meg.
c1-12-01.english: Happen what may, the peaceful protest does not stop. Whatever punishment the authorities may threaten with, we will not back down.
c1-12-01.canDo: I can say that I will not give way, whatever happens (*Történjék bármi, …*).

c1-12-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Why I Refused
c1-12-02.scenario: A friend asks why you refused to sign a document.
c1-12-02.prompt: Say that you refused on grounds of conscience and that your conviction does not allow you to cooperate.
cues: Give the ground of the refusal
c1-12-02.target: Lelkiismereti okból megtagadtam az aláírást. Meggyőződésemtől vezérelve nem működhetek együtt.
c1-12-02.english: I refused to sign on grounds of conscience. Guided by my conviction, I cannot cooperate.
c1-12-02.canDo: I can give the ground of a refusal (*lelkiismereti okból*, *meggyőződéstől vezérelve*).

c1-12-03.title: Communicative Challenge: An Unjust Law
c1-12-03.scenario: A friend asks what the Radbruch formula says about unjust laws.
c1-12-03.prompt: Say that a law can be formally valid and still be statutory injustice, and then it does not count as law.
c1-12-03.target: Bár egy törvény formailag érvényes, mégis lehet törvényes jogtalanság.
c1-12-03.english: Although a law is formally valid, it can still be statutory injustice.
c1-12-03.canDo: I can say what the Radbruch formula claims (*az elviselhetetlenül igazságtalan törvény nem számít jognak*).

c1-12-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Legal, but Accepted?
c1-12-04.scenario: A friend says that a law was passed correctly, so nobody can object to it.
c1-12-04.prompt: Answer that a law can be legal and still lack legitimacy.
cues: Say a law can be legal
c1-12-04.target: Egy törvény lehet legális, miközben híján van a legitimitásnak. A törvények betartása még nem jelenti, hogy az emberek elfogadják a hatalmat.
c1-12-04.english: A law can be legal while lacking legitimacy. Obeying the laws does not yet make power legitimate.
c1-12-04.canDo: I can tell legality from legitimacy (*legalitás*, *legitimitás*).

c1-12-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Text Says About Antipolitics
c1-12-05.scenario: You have read a short text about Konrád György, and a friend asks what it says about antipolitics.
c1-12-05.prompt: Tell your friend what the text says antipolitics is.
cues: Say who or what it defends
c1-12-05.target: A szöveg szerint az antipolitika a civil társadalom önvédelme az államhatalom túlterjeszkedésével szemben.
c1-12-05.english: According to the text, antipolitics is the self-defence of civil society against the overreach of state power.
c1-12-05.canDo: I can report what a text says about a writer's idea (*Konrád szerint …*).

c1-12-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Whatever Happens
c1-12-consolidation.scenario: A friend asks what you would say if you were ordered to do something against your conscience.
c1-12-consolidation.prompt: Say that, whatever happens, you will not cooperate, for reasons of conscience.
c1-12-consolidation.target: Történjék bármi, lelkiismereti okból nem működöm együtt.
c1-12-consolidation.english: Happen what may, I will not cooperate, on grounds of conscience.
c1-12-consolidation.canDo: I can say what I will not give up, whatever happens (*Történjék bármi, …*).
